subject: Next steps: deployment mode selection & migration from legacy GPU clusters
messages:
From: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@acmeai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — infra constraints

Thanks Rachel — good call earlier. Quick clarifications from our side before we lock next steps: 

1) Production latency target: 100–150ms p95 for our retrieval-augmented generation flows.
2) Current infra: two-year-old on-prem NVIDIA cluster (A100-ish), K8s overlay, custom scaler. We also have a handful of requests hitting a third-party hosted API (we currently pay per-token) that we want to phase out in 3–6 months.
3) Data residency: training data and user PII must stay in our VPC; some derivative logs can be routed to a managed service if encrypted.

Questions:
- If we go Dedicated with Redwood, how much work for us to keep traffic inside our VPC? Can Dedicated be fronted by our ingress?
- For Private (VPC/on-prem), what parts of control plane run locally vs Redwood-managed?
- Migration path: is there a recommended sequence for moving from hosted API -> dedicated -> private, or do you recommend skipping hosted for us given residency needs?

Also — can you send a short checklist for migration from legacy GPU clusters (what we need to change in model packaging, container runtime, and KV cache handling)?

Thanks,
Kyle
Director of ML Engineering — AcmeAI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@acmeai.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acmeai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — infra constraints

Kyle — great questions, and thanks for the clear constraints. Recap + concrete answers below, plus proposed next steps. Please reply if anything needs correction.

Recap of constraints you confirmed:
- Target p95: 100–150ms
- On-prem legacy GPU cluster (A100-era), K8s overlay
- Short-term: retire third-party hosted API in 3–6 months
- Data residency: PII must remain in your VPC

Short answers to your questions:
- Dedicated + VPC ingress: Yes. Redwood Dedicated can be deployed in a colocated model where traffic fronting (ingress) terminates in your network and routes to a dedicated pool. Our network engineers work with yours to validate NAT/peering and egress rules. Minimal code changes required: usually an inbound route + auth token rotation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane split: The control plane can be configured in two modes — managed control plane (Redwood-hosted) with customer VPC connectors for data path, or customer-hosted control plane where we provide the control-plane container images and orchestration templates (recommended for air-gapped setups). We will share the exact process matrix.
- Migration sequence recommendation: For your constraints, we typically recommend a two-step approach:
  1) Move inference traffic from the third-party hosted API to Redwood Hosted API for quick wins (low friction) while benchmarking cost/latency.
  2) Parallel work to prep Dedicated or Private (depending on security timeline): spin up a Dedicated proof-of-concept in your cloud/VPC, validate latency and KV cache behavior, then cutover production once SLA and residency checks pass.

Why not skip Hosted? Hosted lets you validate model variants, token economics, and hot-path latency without immediate infra commitments. But if you need strict data residency day-one, Dedicated with private ingress or customer-hosted Private are both valid initial options.

Migration checklist (high level):
- Model packaging: containerized artifacts + runtime version pinning (we recommend our Redwood base image).
- KV cache: move from local filesystem-backed caches to centralized KV service (Redis/Postgres) or Redwood-managed KV cache if you want cross-pod warm starts.
- Tokenization: ensure tokenizer versions match reference; sub-tokenization mismatches are the most common root cause of semantics drift during migration.
- Monitoring: instrument per-request traces and token-level cost logging (we’ll provide a sidecar tracing example).

Attachments I’m sending: Redwood migration playbook v0.9 + template Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for AcmeAI. Links to SOC2 summary and a sample Dedicated sizing worksheet included below.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marcus to run a short latency/cost benchmark against a Hosted test endpoint (we can mirror your current model variant) — target by 2026-12-15
2) Internal kickoff (technical) to scope Dedicated/Private requirements — target week of 2026-12-20
3) Share Mutual Action Plan and proposal for Dedicated sizing — Rachel to update MAP and share DocuSign by 2026-12-17

Available times this week for a 30m follow-up: Thu 12/10 10–11am PT, Fri 12/11 1–3pm PT. Which works?

Thanks — will get the two attachments + links across now.

—

From: Priya Desai <priya@acmeai.com>

Date: 2026-12-09T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — infra constraints

Rachel — thanks for the detailed checklist. A couple of clarifications from my end (security/compliance):

- We cannot permit any PII egress to third-party managed KV caches unless encrypted and with a JWE envelope. Is Redwood able to support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping?
- For the control-plane split, our preference is a customer-hosted control plane (we have an internal ops team). Can you provide the minimum required surface area and a list of images/configs we need to run your control plane in air-gapped mode?

Also — Kyle and I prefer the following cadence: Marcus runs the benchmark against Hosted only if we see parity in encryption/ingress behavior. If not, we’d prefer to go straight to Dedicated POC.

Thanks,
Priya
CTO, AcmeAI

Internal note — looping Marcus and Rachel. Summary and asks for Marcus before the POC: 

1) Benchmark plan (Marcus):
   - Spin up hosted test endpoint using their current model family (we have their model hash from the call). 50 concurrent users, measure p50/p95 for 512-token context. Run with and without prefix KV cache to simulate cold start.
   - Test encryption envelope: verify JWE wrapping to a mock customer KMS and measure overhead.
2) Dedicated sizing (Rachel + Marcus):
   - Use their current throughput profile (avg 120 req/min, burst to 350) and latency target to produce two capacity sketches: 99th percentile cost-optimized and latency-optimized.
3) Private/on-prem checklist (Marcus):
   - Prepare control-plane container list and a short runbook for air-gapped install. Focus on: control-plane API, agent images, runtime image, and sidecar tracing collector.

Deliverables and deadlines: Marcus to share initial benchmark results and control-plane image manifest by 2026-12-15. Rachel to update MAP and draft Dedicated SOW by 2026-12-17.

Keep this internal thread for coordination; share customer-facing summary once we have Marcus’s numbers.
